heroSub: From the coastal dunes of Rockingham to inland Kwinana, we put home owners in touch with an independent structural engineer for walls, cracks, extensions and patio certificates. Call (08) 5550 6237 and find out first whether you need one at all.
introHtml:
Rockingham and Kwinana are two fast-growing council areas on Perth's south-west coast. The ABS put the City of Rockingham at 159,934 people in June 2025, up 3.2% in a year, and the City of Kwinana at 57,422, up 4.6%, the fastest percentage growth of any council area we cover. More people means more patios, carports, extensions and walls coming out, and more owners staring at a new crack wondering what it means.

Kings Park Structural Co is a referral service and paid advertising for independent structural engineers. We pass your enquiry to an independent structural engineering firm, which quotes you and contracts with you directly. We don't inspect, design or certify anything ourselves, and we'll tell you straight when a job may not need an engineer at all.

services.title: Wall removal and beam design
services.desc: Taking out a wall for an open-plan kitchen needs a building permit if the wall supports anything else. The engineer who quotes your job checks what the wall carries and designs the beam, posts and footings your builder installs.

services.title: Crack and structural inspection reports
services.desc: Cracks in brickwork, render or cornices near the coast can have several causes, including water washing sand out from under footings. An independent structural engineer looks at the pattern and writes a report, which is a different thing from a pre-purchase building inspection.

services.title: Extension and second-storey engineering
services.desc: Any change in floor area or height needs a permit, and the City of Rockingham's list for owner-lodged (BA2) applications asks for a structural engineer's details. The engineer who quotes your job prepares those for your builder or building surveyor.

services.title: Patio, carport and shed certificates
services.desc: Patios and carports are everywhere in Rockingham and Kwinana, and a roofed patio is not an exempt pergola. An independent engineer can prepare site-specific drawings, footing design and wind calculations for the council application.

sections.heading: Coastal sand, salt air and what they mean for your house
sections.html:
Geoscience Australia maps the Quindalup dunes along the ocean side of this corridor, with Spearwood sand, a slightly limey dune sand over Tamala Limestone, further inland. Nobody publishes soil mapping street by street, so the only honest answer for your block comes from a site check. A Perth geotechnical firm says most metro sand is Class A under AS 2870, but soft or loose sand is Class P, and that changes the footing design.

Sand has its own weak spot. CSIRO notes that sandy soil is particularly easy to wash away, so a leaking pipe, a downpipe that isn't connected or an overwatered garden bed can undermine a footing. Near the coast, WA building inspectors also see steel lintels rusting above windows and doors, with the rust swelling enough to crack the brickwork around them.

None of that tells you what your crack is. It does explain why an engineer asks about plumbing, reticulation and lintels before offering a view. If you're worried, call (08) 5550 6237 or read more about crack and structural inspections.

sections.heading: Permits in the City of Rockingham and City of Kwinana
sections.html:
For houses, your local council is the permit authority, so Rockingham or Kwinana assesses the application depending on where you live. There are two routes. A certified application (BA1) comes with a Certificate of Design Compliance from a registered private building surveyor and has a statutory decision time of 10 business days; an uncertified application (BA2) is checked by the council's own surveyors and has 25 business days.

The City of Rockingham's guide lists the structural engineer's details, designed and certified by a practising structural engineer, among the BA2 documents. The clock stops whenever the council asks for more information, which is why half-finished engineering slows a job down. The state permit fee is 0.19% of the estimated value of the work for a certified Class 1 or 10 application, or 0.32% uncertified, with a minimum of $121.00; the value is counted including GST.

For what patios and sheds need, see patio, carport and shed certificates. For walls, see wall removal engineering, and for bigger jobs, extension engineering.

sections.heading: What it costs, and who you're dealing with
sections.html:
Most Perth engineering firms quote each job rather than publish a price, and we won't make one up. The fee depends on the house, the structure and what the council needs, so the engineer quotes after seeing photos, plans or the site. Our Perth structural engineer cost guide covers the published figures that do exist and what they actually buy you.

WA is bringing structural engineers under a registration scheme. From 1 July 2027 structural engineering work in WA must be done by a registered building engineer, and you can look up any engineer on the DEMIRS Building Engineer Register before you sign. Kings Park Structural Co is not an engineering firm and holds no registration; the firm that quotes you contracts with you directly.

Further up the coast? See Cockburn, Melville and Canning, or head south to Mandurah and Peel.

faq.q: Do I need a building permit for a patio in Rockingham or Kwinana?
faq.a: Usually, if it has a roof. WA's exemption covers a pergola up to 20 m2 and 2.4 m high, and a pergola by definition has no roof, so a roofed patio or carport generally falls outside it. The engineer's certificate that goes with the application covers footings and wind loads. Check your plans with the council before you build.

faq.q: How long does the City of Rockingham take to issue a building permit?
faq.a: The statutory decision time is 10 business days for a certified (BA1) application and 25 business days for an uncertified (BA2) one, and the City of Rockingham states the same. The clock stops if the council asks for more information. Complete engineering details up front are the simplest way to avoid that.

faq.q: How much does a structural engineer cost in Rockingham and Kwinana?
faq.a: No Perth engineering firm we checked publishes a fixed fee for crack reports, beam design or patio certificates. The engineer who quotes your job sets the price after seeing photos, plans or the site. Council permit fees are separate: 0.19% (certified) or 0.32% (uncertified) of the work's value including GST, minimum $121.00.

faq.q: I live near the coast in Rockingham and have cracks above my windows. Is that serious?
faq.a: We can't tell you that, and nobody can over the phone without seeing it. Cracks above openings near the coast can be linked to rusting steel lintels, but they can also come from footing movement or leaks washing out sand. An independent structural engineer can inspect and report. Call (08) 5550 6237 for a quote.
